summary: A 1970 note with brief preliminary notes on the clock at the Augmentation Research Center at SRI. It is part of the early discussion of timing and measurement on the network.

plainLanguage.summary: The ARC clock stores the current date and time separately from a counter for measuring intervals. RFC 34 describes how both values are stored and how often they are updated.

questions: how did the arc clock store absolute time
what was the relative time accumulator
subtitle: How the ARC clock stored absolute time and elapsed-time counts.

tldr.problem: The Augmentation Research Center needed a clock reference that could provide date and time as well as support interval measurements.
tldr.mechanism: The XDS 940 clock stores absolute time in two core words and relative time in a 24-bit accumulator updated at a chosen interval.
tldr.outcome: The note describes the clock's data layout, update rates and stated accuracy; it is a preliminary technical description.

facts.label: Long-term drift
facts.value: No more than 1 second every 250 days

today: The unit metadata records RFC 34 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The note is a preliminary description of the ARC clock dated 26 February 1970.

sections.title: Absolute Time in Two Words
sections.content:
The ARC clock writes absolute time into two adjacent words of XDS 940 core memory. The first word stores month, day and year in binary fields; the second stores hour, minute and second in binary fields.

The two words are written once each second. The note gives ranges for each date and time field.
sections.plainLanguage: Two memory words hold the calendar date and clock time. The first stores the date, and the second stores the hour, minute and second.

sections.title: Relative Time in an Accumulator
sections.content:
Relative time is stored in one core word as the contents of a 24-bit binary accumulator. The update rate can be chosen as once every 100 microseconds or once every millisecond.

The core location is written each time the accumulator is updated.
sections.plainLanguage: A separate counter measures elapsed time instead of storing a date and time. The clock can update this counter at either of the two rates stated in the note.

sections.title: Accuracy and Standby Power
sections.content:
The note anticipates that the initial setting will be accurate to about 1 second relative to WWV. It says oscillator drift should not cause more than 1 second of accumulated error every 250 days.

The oscillator and clock have standby power to maintain accuracy. Variable delays in accessing core memory limit short-term accuracy to about 10 to 20 microseconds.
sections.plainLanguage: The clock is expected to keep close time over long periods and has standby power. Reading memory takes a variable amount of time, which limits short-term accuracy.
